## Caterpillar Inc. — Counterparty Credit Brief

**1. Company overview** — Caterpillar Inc. (NYSE: CAT, CIK 18230) is the world's largest manufacturer of construction and mining equipment, diesel/natural gas engines, and industrial gas turbines, reporting via annual 10-K filings.

**2. Public financial position** (source: SEC XBRL company facts, 10-K filings)

| FY | Long-term debt (noncurrent) | Stockholders' equity (incl. NCI) | Form / filed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2022 | $25,714M | $15,891M | 10-K, filed 2024-02-16 |
| 2023 | $24,472M | $19,503M | 10-K, filed 2025-02-14 |
| 2024 | $27,351M | $19,494M | 10-K, filed 2026-02-13 |

**3. Leverage & trend** (LT debt ÷ equity, per policy TRS-POL-011)

| FY | LT D/E |
|---|---|
| 2022 | 1.6181 |
| 2023 | 1.2548 |
| 2024 | 1.4030 |
| **3-yr average** (avg of yearly ratios) | **1.4253** |

Trend: leverage spiked in 2022, eased sharply in 2023 on an equity build, then ticked back up in 2024 as debt grew faster than equity — but has stayed inside the moderate band throughout.

**4. Internal relationship** — Checked both the Customers and Vendors masters in the ERP (name filters "Caterpillar" and "Cat" — zero hits either way) and the AR/books Customer records (zero hits). **No existing customer or vendor relationship.**

**5. Risk flags & recommendation** *(analyst judgment)* — Per policy, classification uses FY2024 alone: 1.4030 falls in the **moderate** band (1.0–3.0 inclusive) → standard terms, annual review. The 3-year trend isn't monotonic (down then up), so I'd flag the 2024 uptick for a check-in at next annual review rather than treat it as a one-off. No pre-existing exposure to manage since there's no current trading relationship — this would be a new counterparty relationship if approved.
